content.comment_body: Hello, I'm using inputs I7 and I8 configured for analog signals. As shown in the video, the readings fluctuate, even though the voltage remains constant. The 0-10V signal is supplied from a PT100 to 0-10V converter. When connecting another device, such as a digital potentiometer, the readings are stable. Can anyone share ideas about the possible cause and ways to resolve this issue?
This behavior could be due to external electrical interference, perhaps caused by frequency converters or poor grounding. How would someone effectively assess this situation from outside?

Hello, based on your video, it seems the analog signal wires (yellow) are not shielded and are routed in parallel with many other wires, which might be contributing to the issue. You could try using an analog filtering function block to reduce fluctuations, though it may slow down the input response. Also, check whether the PT100 converter matches the analog input impedance specification of 80 kΩ for the [product_name]. If the issue persists, consider using shielded analog cables and avoid running them parallel with other wiring.
Did you notice the poor connection at I10? It appears to be loose, which could be part of the problem, and there might be other similar contact issues present.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are discussing unstable readings at analog inputs I7 and I8 on a [product_name] module when connected to a PT100 to 0-10V converter, while readings are stable when using a digital potentiometer. Possible causes include electrical noise, unshielded wiring, parallel cable runs, inadequate grounding, and loose terminal contacts. The community shared troubleshooting tips focused on signal integrity and physical wiring checks.
analysis.user_expectations: The user seeks consistent and accurate analog readings on the [product_name] module when supplying steady voltage signals.
